data.name: Ranvir
data.long_meaning: Ran- meaning 'Lord' and Vir- meaning 'Thunderbolt'. This name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Rudra' which represents the Hindu God of Violence, Anger, and Storms.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the god of destruction and transformation. It represents power, strength, and courage. It is believed that those named Ranvir are fearless, strong, and protective.
data.numerology_meaning: Signifies new beginnings, leadership, and independence.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ranvir has a strong Hindu cultural impact as it is derived from the name of a powerful Hindu deity, Rudra, symbolizing violence, anger, and destructive power. This name is also believed to signify strength, courage, and determination in Hindu mythology.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ranvir holds great spiritual significance as it is a divine name, invoking the blessings of the Hindu God Rudra, who is known to bestow power, strength, courage, and protection upon his devotees. The name also symbolizes the power of Shiva, the destroyer of negative energies and the embodiment of pure consciousness in Hinduism.

historical_references.reference: Ranvir Singh was a famous Sikh general in the Mughal army during the late 16th and early 17th centuries. He is best known for his role in the Battle of Chandni Chowk (1660) where he led the Sikh forces against the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb.

historical_references.reference: Ranvir Sena, a feudal army of the Maratha Empire, was led by a Hindu Rajput warrior named Ranvir Singh in the mid-18th century. He is known for his victories against the Nizam of Hyderabad and the Mughals, expanding the Maratha Empire in the Deccan region.
historical_references.context: Maratha Empire, Rajput Warrior, Feudal Army, Nizam of Hyderabad, Mughals, Expansion in Deccan Region
